Issue #2160 (hive run 4c1dedd8):
- src/solve.restart-shared.lib.mjs passed no-op setLogFile/getLogFile stubs to five tool
  executors and omitted them entirely for executeClaude, so every restart/watch/auto-merge

  session log unnamed. The real accessors from src/lib.mjs are now forwarded everywhere.
- The rename itself moved to src/session-log-rename.lib.mjs, which reports a named reason
  instead of throwing a TypeError when a caller forgets the accessors.
- src/solve.results.lib.mjs warned "<file> still exists after cleanup" before checking whether
  the file predates the session, producing a false positive immediately followed by
  "existed before this session - keeping pre-existing file". The pre-existence check now runs
  first, so only real leftovers are reported.

…ed cleanup as problems

Issue #2160: the reported hive run logged 23 "⚠️ Tool result error detected" lines that
were all harness blocks ("Blocked: sleep 240 followed by: …") or the AI tool's own Bash
timeout ("Exit code 143"), plus two lines that described something that never happened
("--no-auto-cleanup" was never passed; a long log comment is handled by gh-upload-log).

- classifyToolResultError() marks harness blocks, command timeouts and bare exit codes as
  benign; claude.lib.mjs logs them as ℹ️ and no longer lets them replace the last assistant
  message, so a truncated stream is reported after what the AI actually said.
- solve records that auto-cleanup was defaulted off for a public repository, and the
  "keeping directory" line states that reason instead of naming an unused flag.
- the "log comment too long" line is informational and names the gh-upload-log fallback.
- prompt guidance (all locales) tells the AI to poll with an until-loop instead of a long
  foreground sleep, which is what triggered the harness blocks in the first place.

commits.messageBody:
…ilures

Issue #2160: `hive --all-issues` reported `❌ 4 task(s) failed (completed: 6)` for 4 issues it
never attempted. The repository was public, so solve's auto-cleanup default kept every ~10 GB
workspace; hive checked free disk space once at startup (73.2 GB) and kept dequeuing; by task 7
only 9.8 GB were left and each remaining task died in solve's pre-flight check
(`Insufficient disk space: 10047MB available, 10240MB required`), posted a "Solution Draft Failed"
comment on the target repository's issue, and was counted as a task failure.

- new src/disk-guard.lib.mjs: free-space probe, workspace inventory, and a guard that reclaims
  idle `/tmp/gh-issue-solver-*` workspaces oldest-first. In-flight workspaces (reported by the
  worker's own output), workspaces that are a live process cwd, and recently modified ones are
  never removed; an unreadable /proc or df is treated as "do not touch" / "do not block".
- hive re-checks disk space before every task, waits for in-flight work to release space, and
  requeues the task (bounded deferrals) instead of spawning a solver that cannot start.
- solve exits 75 (EX_TEMPFAIL) with an environment reason for a disk-space pre-flight failure and
  no longer posts a solver-failure comment on the issue; hive maps that code to a deferral.
- hive's startup check reclaims first and exits 75 with an actionable reason instead of
  process.exit(1) from checkSystem's exitOnFailure path.

commits.messageBody:
The end-of-run summary asked GraphQL only for OPEN pull requests, so the six issues whose
drafts --auto-merge had already merged (link-assistant/router #196-#201) were all listed as
"(no PR found)" in the reported run. Reporting now asks for merged and closed drafts too and
shows their state, while --skip-issues-with-prs keeps gating on open PRs only.

Also reorders the two final exits in hive.mjs so genuine task failures are still reported
before the issue #2160 disk-space deferral halt.

Refs #2160
commits.messageHeadline: fix(hive): report merged solution drafts instead of "no PR found"

commits.messageBody:
Issue #2160 (two defects on the same path):

- hive.mjs called cleanupTempDirectories() with no argv in its non---once
  branch. The function returns immediately without argv, so that call could
  never clean anything: a silent no-op that hid missing cleanup from the log.
- The cleanup ran `sudo rm -rf /tmp/* /var/tmp/*`, which also destroys the
  workspaces, lock directories and log files of any concurrent hive/solve run
  on the same host. listCleanableTempEntries() now enumerates the temp roots
  and keeps anything a live process has as cwd (via /proc/<pid>/cwd), anything
  the caller marks protected, and the run's own log file. An unreadable /proc
  keeps everything rather than guessing.

Also downgrades the JSONL deduplication line from a warning to an
informational message: skipping the duplicates is a known upstream Claude Code
accounting quirk (anthropics/claude-code#6805) and is what keeps token totals
correct, so it is not something a human needs to act on.

experiments/issue-2160-command-stream-array-probe.mjs records why passing the
path list as an array to command-stream's `$` is safe (each element becomes its
own argv entry, no word splitting inside an element).

tests/temp-cleanup-2160.test.mjs covers both defects.
commits.messageHeadline: fix(cleanup): make --auto-cleanup effective and safe for concurrent runs
